# Power-Loss Behavior of Strain Wave Mounts

Dimension 2: does a strain wave mount "simply stay where it was" when power
is cut? This tests the core premise of the kill switch. Sources:
[citations](../citations.md).

## Per-mount brake documentation

| Mount | Brake | Axis | Manufacturer statement | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZWO AM5 | Yes | RA only | "Power-oﬀ Brake RA Axis Only" | [29], [30] |
| ZWO AM5 (staff reply) | Yes | RA only | Tech@ZWO: "Only the RA axis has a brake." | [21] |
| ZWO AM3 | Yes | RA only | "the RA axis has brake protection"; DEC drive listed without brake | [31] |
| iOptron HEM27 | Yes ("Electronic friction brake") | Not stated | Brake allows the mount to "safely stop" after power loss | [32] |
| iOptron HAE29/43 | Yes (friction brake) | RA and DEC | "Unique friction brake on both RA and DEC to safely stop movement during a planned or unplanned power interruption." | [34] |
| iOptron HAEc | Yes ("electronic friction brake") | Not stated | "allows the mount to safely stop even after an abrupt power loss" | [35] |
| Pegasus NYX-101 | Yes (locks the motor shaft) | RA only | DEC "does not have a power-off brake"; unbraked axes can speed up "towards the ground" | [36] |
| Rainbow RST-135 | None mentioned in manual | — | "do not turn off the power while the right ascension axis is rotating... The right ascension axis rotates in the direction of gravity" | [37] |
| Rainbow RST-135 (user) | None | Neither axis | w7ay: "My mount does not have a brake in either axis... Anything under 5 kg is not able backdrive it." | [21] |
| Sky-Watcher Wave 150i | None mentioned | — | Manual RA/DEC "locking knobs"; no power-loss statement | [38] |
| MLAstro SAL-33 | Yes ("physical brake") | RA only | DEC "does not, so you avoid letting it move freely when the system is unpowered" (third-party guide) | [39] |

No astro manufacturer document fetched states the brake type (spring-applied
or otherwise). The behavior described ("power-off", engages on failure) fits
a fail-safe brake but does not prove one.

**AM5 teardown (single user, Tier 4).** jetty reports the AM5 brake is "a
spring loaded solenoid brake such that when there is power, the solenoid is
active and allows the stepper to rotate, and when power is off... the brake
is pushed in place" [88]. He lists "Belt failure" among cases where the load
could freewheel [88]. That places the brake on the motor side of the belt;
this is an inference from his wording. A Reddit user (opinion) likewise says "It has a
brake in the RA motor axis" [89]. ZWO's V1.0 manual describes the RA gear as
having an "inbuilt brake" [29]; the 2023 manual revision says the same in
substance (OCR, paraphrased) [91]. The teardown and the manual wording
are not reconciled.

## Observed behavior when unpowered

- AM5: an owner saw a top-heavy scope "start to rotate by itself" on DEC
  after switch-off; ZWO replied that only RA has a brake [21].
- w7ay (same thread): once a strain wave axis moves, the motor armature
  "acts like a flywheel, through a 100:1 reduction" and is hard to stop [21].
- **Only empirical back-drive data point.** On an AM5 with the brake
  removed, 14 lb in the worst RA position: "Powered off and the load didnʼt
  fall. Pushing on it, it moved and it kept going for a few seconds... it
  will never drop fast, but if thereʼs enough weight it will keep going till
  it hits the tripod/pier extension" [88]. This is one unit and one load.
- DEC on the AM5 "has no braking"; if balanced, "it's unlikely to move on
  it's own" [88].
- A Reddit user: "under enough load a strain wave can be back driven" [89].
- AM5N users disagree: "The mount should never drop" (Celerondon) versus
  "there isn't a brake on the dec" (ris242) [40].
- AM5N teardown of a single unit with guiding problems: RA breakaway torque
  was higher than DEC [28]. It may have been defective; this is not a
  general property.
- A user notes that without clutches you cannot push RA by hand when the
  battery dies ("completely dependent on power") [19]. Another poster's
  rhetorical premise is that some strain wave makers fit clutches, without
  naming any [41]. These conflict. None of the strain wave mount manuals
  fetched ([29]–[39]) mentions a clutch.
- Industrial Harmonic Drive actuators use brakes that "hold the motor shaft
  in place when the power is cut off" [66].

## Engineering sources on back-drivability

| Claim | Source | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| "A high ratio harmonic drive is non-backdrivable" | Kazerooni & Ellis 1995 [54] | 1 (abstract only) |
| Strain wave gears "can withstand shock loads of up to five times the rated torque"; no statement on back-driving | Sponsored primer hosted by Harmonic Drive LLC [90] | 2 |
| Strain wave gears are "fundamentally reversible"; "complete self-locking cannot be guaranteed" | Nabtesco [55] | 2 |
| Strain wave gears show "no-load starting torques—particularly in back-driving conditions" (finite, not infinite) | Frontiers review [56] | 1 |
| Backdrivability depends on ratio; brakes or clutches are fitted against crashes | Source Robotics [57] | 3 |
| "Do not rely on gearbox friction as a safety-rated holding function" | Physical AI Lab [59] | 3 |
| Cutting motor power "lets the joint free-fall until something else stops it" | Arcbotix [60] | 3 |
| Robot arm "will drop when powered off" | UR forum [62] | 4 |

**Contradiction.** The 1995 abstract [54] says high-ratio units cannot be
back-driven. The gear maker [55] and the 2020 review [56] say back-driving
takes a finite torque and self-locking is not guaranteed. ZWO and Pegasus
fit RA brakes, and the Pegasus manual warns about unbraked axes [36]. That
is consistent with the second view. The forum claims that the mount "should
never drop" [40] are user opinion.

## Is a hard power cut mid-slew safe?

| Position | Source |
|---|---|
| Safe stop on power loss, via brake | iOptron [32], [34], [35]; Pegasus [36] |
| Do not cut power while RA is rotating | Rainbow [37] |
| Power off with the switch, not by disconnecting cables (no reason given) | SAL-33 guide [39] |
| Holding brakes used as stopping brakes are "potentially damaging"; acceptable only for "infrequent use" | Rockwell [58] |
| Hard brake engagement "injects a torque impulse" into the harmonic drive | ICNavigator [61] |
| "a hard stop from full speed" is a ratcheting cause; ratcheting "happens in a millisecond" | Arcsec [63] |

## Position memory after power loss

| Mount | Behavior | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ZWO AM5/AM5N | "no absolute encoders"; restart from home (forum) | [40] |
| iOptron HAE | "can memorize its R.A. and DEC positions if the mount power is lost during operation, even during high speed slewing" | [34] |
| iOptron HEM27 | Same feature in the ManualsLib copy of the manual; absent from the iOptron-hosted version, so it may depend on revision | [84], [32] |
| Pegasus NYX-101 | FRAM keeps last position; RA brake released only when tracking is enabled | [36] |

## Gaps and Limitations

- No manufacturer data gives DEC drift or drop distance when an unbraked
  axis loses power under a typical imaging load. The only measurement is one
  qualitative brake-removed test [88].
- Brake type and location for ZWO come from one user teardown [88], not
  from ZWO.
- No manufacturer states whether its brake is rated to stop a slewing axis.
- The ZWO PDF at the 2026-03 URL is an AM5 manual (updated 2023-06-19) [91].
  It was read by OCR, pages 1–20 of 26 only, and is used for paraphrase, not
  quotation.
- The Harmonic Drive basics e-book [90] does not address back-drivability.
- The RST-135 supplementary manual returned a login page.
- The Kazerooni paper was read as an abstract only.
